_comment: Guided tour for the integrated burst workflow (the native hub, gui/native.py; the legacy Qt shell reads it too). The steps are the numbered rows of the left rail, so they target 'panel' -- and they WAIT for the user to select the row rather than selecting it for them. Read by chisurf.emtk.help_guide.EmTkGuidedTour.

steps.title: What this window is
steps.text:
A confocal measurement is a long timestamp stream that is mostly background, with occasional bright bursts — one molecule crossing the focus. Everything you want from it is a number computed per burst.

The left list is that pipeline, in the order it has to happen. Eight steps, about two minutes. You press the rows; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: 0 — detector setup and channels first
steps.text: Every burst analysis needs to know which hardware channels map to donor and acceptor detectors, and how excitation pulses (PIE/ALEX) are gated. Configuring it here establishes the setup used across all downstream steps.

await.hint: Select 0. Setup Selection in the list on the left.

steps.title: 1 — the raw files, once
steps.text: Every later step reads what you select here and nothing re-opens anything else. That is the point of putting it first: the pipeline has one source of data, so a result can always be traced back to the file it came from.

await.hint: Select 1. Data Selection in the list on the left.

steps.title: 2 — the step that decides what a burst is
steps.text:
The search slides a window of m photons along the stream and opens a burst where the count rate rises a factor above the local background. Local is what matters: tied to the background estimated nearby, the threshold survives laser power drifting over a long acquisition.

Search permissively and cut on size afterwards. A size cut applied inside the search biases which molecules you ever see.

steps.title: 3 — one lifetime per burst
steps.text:
Burst MLE fits one fluorescence lifetime per burst and detector, with the detectors of step 0 — no setup to repeat here. It is the last required step: once its lifetimes are there, Finish appears beside Next.

BVA and 2CDE — does a burst's FRET efficiency stay steady while it crosses? — run on their own with their defaults as soon as the bursts are there.

steps.title: Advanced
steps.text: Advanced shows every step and every setting: Burst Fusion (merging the bursts of one molecule that left and came back), BVA and 2CDE with their plots, H2MM (a state for every photon) and the split of the MLE by H2MM state, and each tool's detector setup and tables.

steps.title: Next runs the step, >> runs the rest
steps.text:
Next runs the open step where it has a run (Burst Selection searches) and moves on once it has finished. >> walks every remaining pipeline step in order, waiting for each; pressed again it stops after the current one. Fusion (Advanced) is never run by walking past it. Once the last required step is done, Finish closes the workflow (it asks first).

The line beside them says which setup, how many files and which burst folder the later steps read.

steps.title: The background is not a detail
steps.text:
Every corrected quantity is a count minus a background. Get it wrong and E moves for the dim bursts while the bright ones stay put — which looks exactly like a real sub-population, and is the most common way a burst histogram lies.

Estimate it from the measurement itself, not from a blank.

The Background tool is a side tool: tick Advanced to see it in the rail.

steps.title: Until this is done, E is an instrument reading
steps.text:
α, β, γ and δ remove the biases the optics and the dyes put into the raw counts. Before they are set, an efficiency is a number about your microscope; after, it is a number about your molecule and comparable with anyone else's.

The check that catches most errors: the donor-only population must land at E ≈ 0. It is the one answer you know in advance.

Accurate FRET is a side tool: tick Advanced to see it in the rail.

steps.title: Four checks before you believe a histogram
steps.text:
1. Does the burst count survive a factor of two on the threshold? A real population does; an artefact does not.
2. Is donor-only at E ≈ 0 after correction?
3. Does S separate the species? Singly-labelled molecules must leave before anything is read as a distance.
4. Do dim and bright bursts agree? If E drifts with burst size, suspect the background before the biophysics.

Help beside Guide has the long version and the reading list.
